title: Closed subsets of a Noetherian scheme satisfy the minimal condition
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], i.e. locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Then every nonempty set $\mathcal S$ of closed subsets of the underlying topological space of $X$ has a minimal element for inclusion: there is $T_0\in\mathcal S$ such that no $T\in\mathcal S$ satisfies $T\subsetneq T_0$.

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01OZ (label lemma-Noetherian-topology, properties.tex line 496: a Noetherian scheme has a Noetherian underlying space), with Topology, Definition 0051 (label definition-noetherian, topology.tex line 1244: the descending chain condition for closed subsets); the minimal-element form is how the proofs of Cohomology of Schemes 01YF and 01YI use it ('because X is Noetherian we can choose a minimal element')
